Question: Triangle \(ABC\) has side lengths \(AB=5,\) \(BC=6,\) and \(AC=7.\) Two bugs start simultaneously from \(A\) and crawl along the sides of the triangle in opposite directions at the same speed. They meet at point \(D.\) What is \(BD?\)
Solution:
The bugs travel for the same time at the same speed, so they cover equal distances. At their first meeting after leaving \(A\), their two routes together cover the triangle's perimeter once. The perimeter is
\[
5+6+7=18,
\]
so each bug travels \(18\div2=9\) units.

The bug heading toward \(B\) travels \(5\) units along \(AB\), leaving \(9-5=4\) units to travel along \(BC\). Since \(4<6\), the meeting point lies on \(BC\), and \(\boxed{BD=4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
